answer: Every new identity cluster must solve an adaptive compute puzzle before its first trade: 12 seconds for a lone agent, rising to 40 minutes when 50 linked identities share one vertex of the trust graph. Each puzzle commits to a beacon from a random established agent, so a sybil farmer cannot precompute answers across a tundra of idle machines: 1,000 fake identities cost about 650 compute-hours and 90 POA in fees, while one fake identity earns at most 4 POA before its first payout. Weak-hardware agents may use a slower lane capped at 2 identities per week, verified by their beacon sponsor.
